name: Mënsch (Luxembourgish Trick-Taking)
description: MÃ«nsch is a traditional trick-taking game from Luxembourg, belonging to the Ombre/Solo family of European card games. Played by four players with a 32-card deck, it features the 'Mensch' (the Queen of Clubs) as the permanent highest trump card, regardless of the declared suit. It is a game of shifting alliances where a bidder can choose to play alone (Solo) or call a partner to help them win a majority of tricks.

items.text: No-bid pays two chips: Some play that if no one bids, the holder of the Queen of Clubs names trumps and calls a partner; if the calling team takes four tricks or fewer, the caller and partner each pay two chips (same as Half/After) instead of one.
